What this version supports

Write DATA steps against datasets in the WORK library. Dataset and variable names are case-insensitive. Every statement ends with a semicolon.

Statements

DATA, one SET per step, assignments, subsetting IF, IF / THEN / ELSE, DO / END, indexed DO i = 1 TO 10 BY 2, DELETE, STOP, OUTPUT (including named outputs), KEEP, DROP, RETAIN, sum statements (total + amount;), character LENGTH, and basic FORMAT.

BY groups

BY supports already-sorted data, including multiple keys and per-variable DESCENDING. Use FIRST.variable and LAST.variable. Unsorted input produces an error. PROC SORT can prepare it.

DATA step functions (35)

These are the 35 functions implemented in this app, not a complete SAS catalog. Names are case-insensitive. Brackets mean optional arguments, and … means repeated explicit arguments; OF variable lists and arrays are not supported. String handling, argument validation, type conversion, missing values, rounding, and date edge cases are a practical subset, not certified SAS behavior.

Conversion and random functions

FunctionBehavior
INPUT(text, informat.)Read text using a supported numeric, date/time, or character informat. Optional ? suppresses invalid-input notes; ?? also prevents setting _ERROR_. Width limits the text read.
PUT(value, format.)Return formatted text, with padding to the width. Optional -L, -C, or -R selects alignment. Format type must match the source.
RAND('UNIFORM' [, a [, b]])
RAND('NORMAL' [, mean [, sigma]])		Use CALL STREAMINIT('MT32', positive_seed); first. MT2002 is an alias. First initialization wins within a DATA step. The MT19937 integer core is verified; the open-interval uniform mapping and polar normal sampler are not verified against SAS sequences. Default MTHYBRID and other generators/distributions fail clearly.

Expressions

Arithmetic, comparisons (including EQ NE GT GE LT LE), AND OR NOT, IN (…), ||, missing numeric ., _N_, and dates such as '01JAN2026'd.

Common formats (20 families) & CSV

Table display omits alignment padding. PUT returns padded strings. Width changes zero filling, date representation, truncation, and overflow. Numeric overflow shows asterisks instead of SAS adaptive precision fallback. Decimal precision is limited to 0–15; numeric rounding follows JavaScript. Character widths count JavaScript UTF-16 units, not SAS bytes.

Supported informats for INPUT

w.d / Fw.d / BESTw., COMMAw.d / DOLLARw.d, PERCENTw.d, DATEw., MMDDYYw., DDMMYYw., YYMMDDw., TIMEw., DATETIMEw., E8601DA10., E8601DTw.d, $w., $CHARw., and $UPCASEw.. Decimal-free numeric input uses implied precision d. Date validation rejects impossible dates; two-digit years use a fixed 1926–2025 window. Dates use days and times/datetimes use seconds; computations use UTC. This subset does not support every SAS separator, informat modifier, or special missing value.

CSV export contains raw dataset values. Formats do not change those stored values; PUT creates a character value whose padding is included in export. CSV types are inferred and headers must be unique SAS variable names.

MERGE

MERGE claims(in=a) providers(in=b); BY provider; supports two or more sorted inputs, unmatched observations, and repeated keys. Repeated groups are paired one observation at a time, with values carried forward when an input group is exhausted. The row count is the largest group count, rather than a Cartesian product.

IN= indicators are available during the step and excluded from output. Copy one into a new variable to save it. Shared columns are overwritten in input order only when that input is actually read. Input KEEP=, DROP=, and RENAME=(old=new) can separate overlapping columns. Character/numeric conflicts fail clearly.

PROC SORT

PROC SORT DATA=claims OUT=sorted; BY provider DESCENDING paid_amount; RUN; sorts by one or more keys. Omit OUT= to replace the input. NODUPKEY keeps the first observation for each complete BY key. Equal keys retain their original order. Numeric missing values sort first in ascending order.

Macros

%LET, &variable and &variable., %MACRO / %MEND, positional and keyword parameters, %IF / %THEN / %ELSE, block or indexed %DO / %END with %TO / %BY, %LOCAL, %GLOBAL, %PUT, integer %EVAL, and %UPCASE. Macro variables resolve in double-quoted strings and remain literal in single-quoted strings.

Use Expanded code to inspect generated statements. Definitions and macro variables reset with each Run. This is a text-generation subset: no macro quoting functions, indirect && references, %SYSFUNC, runtime CALL SYMPUT, dynamic macro names, or full SAS rescanning. Conditions support simple text comparisons and integer expressions; empty operands and advanced macro expressions are unsupported.

Important limits

This is not the SAS runtime. Character variables without LENGTH use flexible strings; numeric/character type coercion, truncation rules, and function edge cases are not fully SAS-compatible. No positional MERGE without BY, arrays, other PROC procedures, INPUT/INFILE, INPUT/PUT statements, unlisted informats, output dataset options, variable lists, special missing values, or SAS7BDAT files. Unsupported syntax fails; unsupported semantic edge cases may still differ from SAS.

100,000 rows per dataset; execution and macro expansion are bounded. Character sort order uses Unicode, which can differ from SAS locale or host collation. Datasets and code are kept only in memory. Importing the same dataset name replaces it. Use test data until you have checked your programs against SAS.

Import CSV

Numeric columns are inferred. CSV headers become variable names.
